shaving.title: Shaving care
shaving.intro: Based on the American Academy of Dermatology's shaving tips.

steps.label: Soften first
steps.detail: Shave after a warm shower, or wet your skin and hair first so hairs are softer.

steps.label: Use a shaving cream or gel
steps.detail: If your skin is sensitive, choose one made for sensitive skin and check the label for 'fragrance-free'.

steps.label: Shave with the grain
steps.detail: Shave in the direction your hair grows and rinse the blade after each swipe.

steps.label: Replace blades often
steps.detail: A dull blade drags and irritates; change the blade or disposable razor every 5–7 shaves.

steps.label: Moisturise afterwards
steps.detail: Finish with your moisturiser to calm and protect freshly shaved skin.

razor_bumps.title: Razor bumps & ingrown hairs
razor_bumps.intro: Small changes that often reduce bumps. This isn't a diagnosis.

steps.label: Don't stretch the skin
steps.detail: Pulling skin taut while shaving lets hairs retract below the surface, where they can grow back in.

steps.label: Avoid shaving too close
steps.detail: Fewer passes, or a trimmer that leaves a little length, can help.

steps.label: Leave bumps alone
steps.detail: Don't pick or dig at ingrown hairs — that can cause marks and infection.

steps.label: See a dermatologist
steps.detail: If bumps are painful, frequent or leave dark marks, a dermatologist can suggest treatment.

beard.title: Beard-area care
beard.intro: Skin under facial hair still needs cleansing and moisture.

steps.label: Cleanse the beard area
steps.detail: Work your gentle cleanser through the beard to the skin underneath, then rinse well.

steps.label: Moisturise the skin underneath
steps.detail: Massage moisturiser into the skin, not just the hair; a beard oil is optional.

steps.label: Trim on clean, dry hair
steps.detail: Trimming dry hair shows the true length and avoids cutting too short.

workout.title: Sweat & post-workout care
workout.intro: Sweat left on skin can contribute to breakouts for some people.

steps.label: Cleanse after sweating
steps.detail: Wash your face with your gentle cleanser soon after a workout.

steps.label: Change out of sweaty clothes
steps.detail: Especially headbands and caps that sit against the skin.

steps.label: Reapply sunscreen outdoors
steps.detail: If you train outside, reapply after sweating.

outdoors.title: Outdoor protection
outdoors.intro: Daily sunscreen matters most when you're outside for long periods.

steps.label: Reapply sunscreen
steps.detail: Reapply about every two hours outdoors, and after sweating or swimming.

steps.label: Add shade
steps.detail: A wide-brimmed hat or cap and sunglasses add protection.

makeup.title: Makeup removal
makeup.intro: Only relevant because you told us you wear makeup or tinted sunscreen.

steps.label: Remove makeup first
steps.detail: Use a gentle remover such as micellar water or a cleansing balm before your cleanser.

steps.label: Never sleep in makeup
steps.detail: Leftover makeup can clog pores and irritate skin.

steps.label: Sunscreen under makeup
steps.detail: Apply sunscreen as the last skincare step, then let it set before makeup.

cautions.patch_test: Patch-test each new product on a small area (for example, behind the ear or on the inner arm) for a few days before using it on your face.
cautions.one_active: Introduce only one new active ingredient at a time, a couple of weeks apart, so you can tell what suits you.
cautions.sensitive: Because your answers point to sensitivity, we've left out the active treatment serum and kept the routine short.
cautions.many_products: You told us you already use several products. Using many actives together raises the chance of irritation — keep the essentials and add extras one at a time.
cautions.fragrance_free: Look for 'fragrance-free' on labels. 'Unscented' products can still contain masking fragrance.
cautions.dermatologist: See a dermatologist for persistent acne, painful bumps, rashes or anything that worries you.
